desc: The least processed tea: just withered and dried. Delicate, hay-like, subtly sweet.
Heat-fixed immediately after plucking to stop oxidation entirely, preserving a vegetal, grassy profile.
process: Fix (pan-fire or steam) to halt oxidation

desc: Rare and labor-intensive: an extra 'sealed yellowing' step mellows the grassy edge of green tea.
The widest range of any category — partially oxidized, bruised at the edges then fixed, spanning floral-light to dark-roasted.
Fully oxidized until the leaf turns dark and the flavor turns malty, brisk, or fruity depending on origin.
Aged and fermented by microbes rather than simply oxidized — flavor deepens and changes for years, even decades.
brew: 95–100°C · rinse first steep, then short steeps
